detail.abstract: Blockchain-based voting systems provide transparency and auditability but introduce significant privacy risks due to publicly observable metadata. Existing approaches rely on mixnets or heavy cryptographic primitives to achieve anonymity, resulting in high computational overhead and limited scalability. In this paper, we propose a novel privacy-preserving voting protocol that eliminates the need for full ciphertext mixnets by introducing a selective metadata mixing mechanism. Our protocol combines zero-knowledge proofs for vote validity, homomorphic encryption for confidential aggregation, and randomized metadata transformations to achieve unlinkability. We formalize security properties including ballot secrecy, unlinkability, and end-to-end verifiability, and prove security under standard cryptographic assumptions. We further provide a gas-aware smart contract model and evaluate scalability for elections with one million voters under Layer-2 rollup deployment. Our results show that the proposed protocol reduces anonymization complexity from O(n log n) to O(n) while maintaining strong privacy guarantees.

title: QR Navigation Security Is Not Primarily a Cryptography Problem: A Trust-Model Framework for Managed Issuer Verification, Destination Binding, and Runtime Safety

detail.title: QR Navigation Security Is Not Primarily a Cryptography Problem: A Trust-Model Framework for Managed Issuer Verification, Destination Binding, and Runtime Safety

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No competing financial or personal interests relevant to this work.

detail.abstract: Navigation QR codes are now widely used across payments, ordering, public-facing navigation, and other business or institutional workflows, yet current mainstream QR scanning appears to remain primarily a convenience feature rather than a trust system. This paper addresses navigation QR rather than presentation or credential QR. Scanners typically decode a payload and surface a URL or app intent, but do not determine whether the issuer is legitimate, whether the destination remains issuer-approved, or whether the destination is safe at the time of scanning. The central claim of this manuscript is that navigation-QR security is not primarily a cryptography problem. Signed payloads, certificate checks, and HTTPS transport are necessary but insufficient because they do not, by themselves, create a managed trust signal for users. The framework developed here separates issuer legitimacy, destination binding, and runtime destination safety; develops one hierarchical but federated trust-tree model for issuer delegation and state distribution; defines issuer assurance tiers and scanner decision states; and analyzes enrollment, inspection scope, and governance constraints. It does not claim a completed deployment or empirical validation of a universal governance model. Instead, it argues that the surveyed platform behavior and cited literature do not show a widely deployed managed trust layer that can make scanner-visible trust states intelligible to users.

title: Operator Homogenization via the Exp-Minus-Log (EML) Function: Increasing Analysis Costs through Representation Uniformity

detail.title: Operator Homogenization via the Exp-Minus-Log (EML) Function: Increasing Analysis Costs through Representation Uniformity
detail.abstract: We investigate operator homogenization, a code transformation strategy that rewrites heterogeneous program expressions into recursive compositions of the single Exp-Minus-Log (EML) operator eml(x, y) = exp(x)-ln(y)tivated by recent symbolic manipulation studies that treat EML as a unified expression primitive, we examine the impact of this structural uniformity on reverse engineering effort across three domains: cryptographic software, anti-cheat integrity checks, and malware analysis. Our transformation collapses operator-type diversity within expressions, reducing the effectiveness of common pattern-based heuristics used in static analysis. We introduce empirical metrics-Operator Obfuscation Ratio (OOR) and Depth Expansion Factor (DEF)-to quantify the structural distortion induced by homogenization. In evaluations against YARA signature scanners, IDA Pro FLIRT library identification, and the angr symbolic executor, we observe the elimination of standard library signatures and a 5-9× increase in symbolic path exploration time. We make no claims of cryptographic security or bit-level semantic preservation. Our findings indicate that operator homogenization constitutes a practical and underexplored axis for increasing the costs associated with software reverse engineering.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a governance theory of evaluation based on evaluative entitlement. Moving beyond prior work treating entitlement as a static condition, entitlement is theorized as a governance mechanism that coordinates how evaluative rights are allocated and which evaluations are admitted. Three mechanisms are specified-assignment (who evaluates), constraint (what is evaluated), and enforcement (whether evaluation is admitted)-and their joint effects theorized: substitution, reinforcement, and conflict. The paper makes three contributions. First, evaluation is reframed as a governed decision right rather than informational input, shifting attention from signal quality to authority structure. Second, evaluative entitlement is transformed from a descriptive condition into an explanatory governance mechanism. Third, input governance is established as a necessary but often overlooked condition for system validity, with direct implications for IS design, Responsible AI, and evaluation systems. The paper concludes by deriving eight testable propositions to guide empirical research.

detail.abstract:
This theory-building conceptual paper proposes the Internet of Products (IoP) as the third major stage of internet infrastructure evolution — following the Internet of Information and the Internet of Value. It introduces a new Product Identity Layer in which every physical product is assigned a persistent, verifiable, and network-accessible digital identity, enabling it to function as an active economic entity across its entire lifecycle.

Drawing on transaction cost theory, information asymmetry theory, and digital infrastructure theory, the paper develops the 4E Model of Product Digitisation (Encode → Enrich → Exchange → Execute) with explicit boundary conditions and failure-mode analysis. Six research propositions are formulated, five of which are refined into testable hypotheses with operationalised constructs and identified data sources. The framework is grounded through three illustrative cases (EU Falsified Medicines Directive, Parmigiano Reggiano RFID authentication, and Homie Product-as-a-Service) and critically examines key challenges including the oracle problem, governance failures (TradeLens), and privacy-transparency tensions.

Theoretical contributions are threefold: (1) positioning IoP as a categorically distinct infrastructure layer due to the physical-digital linkage (oracle) challenge; (2) the 4E Model as a staged framework with boundary conditions and failure modes; (3) generating cross-stream predictions by integrating previously fragmented literatures (IoT, supply chain, DPP, digital twins, and tokenisation) under a unified infrastructure-theoretic lens.

The paper concludes with a structured research agenda for empirical validation. This version is targeted at Electronic Markets (Springer) and represents a substantially revised and improved manuscript.

Keywords: Internet of Products, Product Identity Layer, Digital Infrastructure, 4E Model, Digital Product Passport, Real-World Assets, Tokenization, Transaction Cost Theory, Information Asymmetry, Oracle Problem

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a simple phonological encoding system that maps digits (0-9) into structured consonant-vowel sound units. The goal is to transform numerical sequences into pronounceable patterns that are easier to remember. Each digit is assigned a consonant and a vowel. Numbers are encoded using a strict consonant-vowel (CV) alternation rule. Arithmetic results are first computed normally, then converted into phonological form. Unlike previous mnemonic systems, this method preserves full reversibility, strict structural consistency, and minimal rule complexity.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a formal mathematical specification of the Unified Emotional Responsibility Architecture (U.E.R.A.), the behavioral control framework underlying AkaneCore. Building on the conceptual and empirical findings of Papers I through III in this series, we define the core constructs-state space, responsibility trigger function, response generation constraints, state transition, and emotion-weighted memory filtering-within a probabilistic and control-theoretic framework. The principal contributions are threefold. First, the Knowledge-Action Gap is reformulated as a quantifiable probabilistic divergence. Second, responsibility triggers are defined as logical functions with persona-specific sensitivity parameters, enabling precise specification of constraint activation conditions. Third, the Emotion-Weighted Memory Filtering System (EW-MFS) is described as a formal memory management function with explicit classification rules. Through this formalization, U.E.R.A. is elevated from an intuitive design philosophy to a verifiable theoretical framework with testable predictions.

detail.abstract: In today's world, the business environment is continuously changing, becoming more complex and tough, and such firms require advanced people that are eager to learn, execute, adapt and have a positive attitude. Self-efficacy generally makes a decision the way a person feels, thinks, act and is proved to be a constructive feeling supplying the capability to deal with a diffusion of stressors. Resilience assists people in coping with adversity, maintaining successful contact, and experiencing pleasant emotions. The essence of this research is to determine the amount of self-efficacy and resilience among generation Z employees, as well as the link between the two. Having recognized the extent of self-efficacy and resilience we were able to realize the strategies era Z adapt to address pressure. The data for the study was collected using a structured questionnaire. The major findings reveal that self-efficacy and resilience do not significantly affect work performance, it is implied that additional abilities are required for success in addition to these two.

title: EDMD: A Unified Event-Driven Medallion Architecture with Domain-Driven Design for Real-Time Credit Risk Feature Engineering
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: EDMD: A Unified Event-Driven Medallion Architecture with Domain-Driven Design for Real-Time Credit Risk Feature Engineering
detail.abstract: Highlights • EDMD formally integrates event-driven processing, DDD bounded contexts, and an extended four-tier Medallion architecture into a unified production ML feature engineering framework. • A novel Platinum tier extends the standard Medallion architecture with model-ready, governance-embedded, drift-monitored features achieving zero training-serving skew by construction. • Formal watermark strategies for late-arriving financial events are derived and validated: transactions (15 min), payments (72h), bureau (30d), account changes (24h). • Domain anti-corruption layers enforce strict bounded context isolation, eliminating cross-domain data leakage-critical for SR 11-7 and BCBS 239 compliance. • Synthetic benchmarks at 10M events/day demonstrate 99.7% late-event recovery versus 61.3% for Lambda architecture, with TSS=0 by construction.

title: Religious Signaling and Consumer Trust in Bangladesh's Facebook Commerce: A Generational Perspective
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Religious Signaling and Consumer Trust in Bangladesh's Facebook Commerce: A Generational Perspective
detail.abstract: This study examines how religious signaling influences consumer trust and purchase behavior within Bangladesh's Facebook-based commerce (f-commerce) ecosystem. Drawing on signaling theory, the Elaboration Liked Model (ELM), and social commerce trust frameworks, the research combines a structured survey of 400 respondents across four generational cohorts with five scenario-based choice experiments. Customer reviews emerged as the dominant trust driver (69% of respondents), while religious endorsement ranked last at 5%. Chi-square tests confirmed significant generational differences (χ² = 47.3, df = 6, p < .001): consumers aged 35 and above were substantially more responsive to religious cues, whereas Gen Z and younger millennials relied predominantly on reviews and verifiable information. Binary logistic regression identified customer reviews (OR = 4.21, p < .001) and seller professionalism (OR = 2.87, p < .001) as the strongest independent predictors of purchase intention, while religious cue exposure was non-significant after controls (OR = 1.21, p = .251). These findings extend and contextualise Islam et al.'s (2023) demonstration that religious belief predicts halal purchase intention in formal branded product contexts, showing that this effect is suppressed in informal digital commerce when consumer reviews are present. The study reconceptualises religious signaling as a secondary, context-dependent trust mechanism within a multi-layered hierarchy, with implications for digital marketing practice, consumer protection policy, and the study of religion in informal digital markets.

title:
Влияние санкционного давления на цифровую трансформацию вертикально интегрированных нефтегазовых компаний России


The impact of sanctions pressure on the digital transformation of Russia’s vertically integrated oil and gas companies

detail.title:
Влияние санкционного давления на цифровую трансформацию вертикально интегрированных нефтегазовых компаний России


The impact of sanctions pressure on the digital transformation of Russia’s vertically integrated oil and gas companies
detail.abstract:
Аннотация

В статье анализируется влияние санкционного давления на процессы цифровой трансформации вертикально интегрированных нефтегазовых компаний (далее – ВИНК) России. В работе также рассматриваются институциональные, технологические и управленческие последствия ограничений, обусловленных внешнеполитической средой, а также особенности адаптации компаний к новым условиям. В настоящей сатье также показано, что санкции одновременно выступают барьером и, одновременно, элементом развития цифровых преобразований, стимулируя ускоренное импортозамещение, развитие отечественных технологий и пересборку цифровой архитектуры ВИНК.

Обобщены ключевые направления трансформации: переход на российские цифровые платформы, повышение уровня кибербезопасности, перестройка цепочек поставок технологического оборудования и формирование новой управленческой модели цифрового развития.

Abstract

The article examines the impact of sanctions pressure on the digital transformation processes of vertically integrated oil and gas companies (VIOCs) in Russia. It highlights the institutional, technological, and managerial consequences of external restrictions, along with the strategies adopted by VIOCs to adapt to the new geopolitical context. The study demonstrates that sanctions act both as a barrier and as a catalyst for digital transformation, accelerating import substitution, promoting the development of domestic technologies, and reshaping the digital architecture of Russian VIOCs. Key transformation directions are identified, including the transition to Russian digital platforms, strengthening cybersecurity, restructuring technological supply chains, and forming a new managerial model for digital development.

title: CSR Communications: Impact of Corporate Social Responsibility Activities on Shaping the Skill Development of Workforce in India
affiliations: Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Institute of Management Technology & Research, Dhanwate National College, Nagpur

detail.title: CSR Communications: Impact of Corporate Social Responsibility Activities on Shaping the Skill Development of Workforce in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study was conducted in accordance with ethical standards. Informed consent was obtained from all participants, and their confidentiality and anonymity were maintained.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this study.

detail.abstract: The role of corporate social responsibility (CSR) is to actively contribute to the socio-economic development of communities, enabling individuals and society to achieve sustainable progress along with contentment. However, students from economically weaker sections, as well as physically and socially challenged groups, have often been marginally excluded from employment opportunities due to a lack of skills and confidence in many organisations. Despite the provision of job opportunities to individuals from the lower socio-economic strata, CSR initiatives often result in short-term income generation without fostering long-term social mobility or measurable financial advancement—unless implemented wholeheartedly and with genuine commitment by all stakeholders. This study investigates the role of CSR activities, when effectively communicated, in enhancing the skill development of employees and the potential workforce in India. The research focuses on CSR initiatives in education, vocational training, digital literacy, and up skilling programs, exploring how communication strategies influence participation, learning outcomes, and employability. Analysis of secondary data from various companies across industries reveals that transparent and participative CSR communication fosters higher engagement in skill-building programs and better alignment of skills with industry needs.

title: Parasocial Trust Transfer: Creators, Influencers, and the Connection Variable in the Customer Trust Equation

detail.title: Parasocial Trust Transfer: Creators, Influencers, and the Connection Variable in the Customer Trust Equation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Christina Garnett is the originator of the Customer Trust Infrastructure framework and the Customer Trust Equation referenced in this paper. No other competing interests are declared.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This manuscript presents a conceptual framework and does not report on research involving human participants, animals, or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for the preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: Brands invest heavily in creator and influencer partnerships; however, the structural conditions under which these partnerships build or destroy trust remain poorly understood. This paper argues that creators and influencers function as trust infrastructure: actors whose parasocial relationships with audiences directly activate the Connection variable of the Customer Trust Equation (Trust = Consistency + Response + Connection + Value-Friction). Drawing on parasocial interaction theory, Goffman's dramaturgical account of self-presentation, and Abidin's concept of communicative intimacies, influencer-brand partnerships succeed or fail according to whether they sustain or disrupt the conditions for connection, and friction, the equation's sole subtractive force, is most acutely introduced when authenticity collapses. This framework provides practitioners with a structural vocabulary for influencer selection and partnership design and provides researchers with a component-level model for theorizing and measuring influencer efficacy. Managerial implications are developed across four imperatives: evaluating influencer relational infrastructure, auditing the brand's own trust variables, identifying friction risk before launch, and recognizing the asymmetry of relational risk between creators and brands.

title: Graph-Theoretic Approaches to Hierarchical Revenue Target Allocation in B2B Enterprises: A Methodological Framework

detail.title: Graph-Theoretic Approaches to Hierarchical Revenue Target Allocation in B2B Enterprises: A Methodological Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is employed by Atlassian. This research was conducted independently and does not represent the views, opinions, or endorsement of Atlassian. The author declares no financial or competing interests related to this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses only synthetic data generated for methodological demonstration. No human subjects, proprietary data, or confidential information were used.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Enterprise B2B revenue forecasting operates under structural constraints absent from standard time-series and regression frameworks. Corporate targets are established at the organizational apex and must be deterministically cascaded through multi-layered management hierarchies, where each layer independently applies safety buffers ("managerial hedges") that compound down the tree. Furthermore, human forecast submissions ("commits") introduce systematic behavioral biases-sandbagging and optimism-that existing machine learning libraries cannot reconcile. This paper presents a graph-theoretic framework that models organizational reporting structures as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) using NetworkX, enabling: (1) top-down quota cascading weighted by historical node capacity with configurable hedge multipliers, (2) behavioral bias quantification via a computed Bias Index that reconciles human commits against historical actuals, and (3) post-allocation pipeline health diagnosis with zero-sum quota redistribution among individual contributors based on real-time pipeline coverage ratios. We demonstrate through numerical experiments on synthetic enterprise hierarchies that traditional forecasting tools (Meta Prophet, Scikit-Learn Random Forests) produce structurally incoherent allocations under hierarchical constraints, while the proposed DAG-based approach preserves mathematical consistency across all organizational levels. The framework has been implemented as an open-source Python package (b2b-revenue-forecasting) available on PyPI.

title: Hegemony Groupality and Civil Groupality (民心集格): A 2×2 Matrix of Progressive–Conservative × Heg-leaning/Civ-leaning ── A New Paradigm of Simup Sasang

detail.title: Hegemony Groupality and Civil Groupality (民心集格): A 2×2 Matrix of Progressive–Conservative × Heg-leaning/Civ-leaning ── A New Paradigm of Simup Sasang
detail.abstract: This Working Paper introduces a new paradigm of Simup Sasang for analyzing collective political-economic dynamics. Built on the Theory of Groupality (Sim 2026, SSRN 6663558), the paradigm proposes a structural reframing: discard the Left–Right frame as an eighteenth-century parliamentary-geographic vocabulary insufficient for twenty-first-century analysis, preserve the Progressive–Conservative frame as a temporality-of-change vocabulary, and add a structural dimension of Heg-leaning (覇派, vested-interest oriented) versus Civ-leaning (民派, popular-heart oriented). The combination yields a 2×2 matrix with four positions: Progressive–Heg, Progressive–Civ, Conservative–Heg, and Conservative–Civ. The paper develops five contributions. First, the analytic case for discarding the Left–Right frame and preserving Progressive–Conservative. Second, a genealogical foundation tracing Heg-leaning and Civ-leaning to Paleolithic Fairness Sense (PFS) and post-agricultural surplus differentiation, anchoring both dimensions in human evolutionary history rather than modern ideology. Third, precise definitions of Hegemony Groupality (HG) ── collective entities operating through hierarchical concentration, asymmetric responsiveness, selective memory, and self-perpetuating reproduction ── and Civil Groupality (CG, 民心集格) ── collective entities operating through participatory deliberation, distributed accountability, and reciprocal recognition. Fourth, empirical applications to AI governance, financial markets, and political institutions. Fifth, methodological implications for accountability frameworks, particularly the Network Liability Matrix (NLM) and the Reputation Information Sharing Platform (GRISP). The decisive analytic insight is that the 2×2 matrix makes visible what the Left–Right frame conceals: both progressives and conservatives can be Heg-leaning, and both progressives and conservatives can be Civ-leaning. The Simup Sasang entry-point for political-economic analysis is therefore not "which party does the actor belong to" but "in which of the four quadrants does the actor operate." The paradigm is offered as a contribution to comparative political-economy, social ontology, and AI governance research, in dialogue with critical-theory traditions while adding a Groupality-grounded structural analytic. This paper is part of the Simup Sasang research program. Related papers in the series: Sim (2026) "A Theory of Groupality" (SSRN 6663558); Sim (2026) "The Upper-Level Reference Point Principle" (SSRN 6551498); Sim (2026) "Groupality Index and Wartime Defense Contracts" (SSRN 6595078); Sim (2026) "AI Stock Bubble Is Designed" (SSRN 6551159); Sim (2026) "Price Has No Reference Point" (SSRN 6462160).

title: When Culture Plays the Game: Introducing The Culture Oriented Gamification Marketing Framework

detail.title: When Culture Plays the Game: Introducing The Culture Oriented Gamification Marketing Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants or patient data and therefore ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: While gamification has been widely adopted in marketing to enhance customer engagement and brand interaction and loyalty, existing frameworks often emphasize motivational and behavioral mechanisms without adequately accounting for cultural variability in consumer response. This conceptual paper addresses this less developed aspect by positioning cultural context as a central determinant of how consumers interact with gamified marketing strategies. It introduces the Culture Oriented Gamification Framework (COGAM), a conceptual framework that integrates Hofstede's six cultural dimensions with the Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics/Emotions (MDA/MDE) model to deepen the understanding of how cultural context shapes consumer perception, engagement, and emotional response, thereby advancing culturally adaptive gamification marketing design. COGAM is represented as three layers corresponding to the MDA/MDE framework-Mechanics (rules, systems, and structures), Dynamics (behaviors and interactions), and Aesthetics/Emotions (subjective and affective experiences)-intersected by twelve cultural dimensions representing the high and low poles of Hofstede's six cultural dimensions. By fusing these two theoretical lenses, COGAM translates abstract cultural attributes such as power distance, individualism-collectivism, masculinity-femininity, uncertainty avoidance, long-short-term orientation, and indulgencerestraint into actionable gamified marketing strategies.

title: Using LLM-Based Priors to Optimize Choice Designs in Conjoint Experiments
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School - Department of Marketing and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Using LLM-Based Priors to Optimize Choice Designs in Conjoint Experiments
detail.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used in marketing research to simulate consumers or augment human data. This paper examines a different role for large language models (LLMs): Using them as a source of prior utility information to improve choice-based conjoint (CBC) experiments before collecting data from consumers. We define LLM-generated priors as directly elicited expectations about conjoint part-worth utilities, distinct from synthetic choices or digital twins that substitute for respondent answers. In a CBC study of premium job-search platform subscriptions with 984 U.S. job seekers, we compare a conventional randomized design with LLM-optimized designs based on aggregate, individualized, and deliberately misspecified priors. We show that LLM-generated priors alone predict holdout choices beyond chance and, when used to screen out dominated choice tasks, improve predictive performance substantially. Integrating LLM priors in subsequent empirical Bayes and hierarchical Bayes estimation yields mixed additional benefits. Diagnostic and sensitivity analyses across additional conjoint applications identify four dimensions that LLMs can target to improve the accuracy of utility priors. The findings position LLMs not as substitutes for human data, but as scalable input of approximate prior structure for designing more informative choice experiments for consumers.

title: The Algorithm Doesn't Know What You Love: An Inquiry into Recommendation Systems, Conversational Coordination, and the Constraint-Variance Ratio
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Algorithm Doesn't Know What You Love: An Inquiry into Recommendation Systems, Conversational Coordination, and the Constraint-Variance Ratio
detail.abstract: Recommendation systems surface content based on behavioral residue: plays, skips, dwell time, co-viewing patterns. Less examined is the structural relationship between what these systems measure and what a person actually experiences as discovery. This paper offers an inquiry into that gap. Drawing on the Coordination Invariant framework (S = C/V)-which proposes that adaptive systems maintain coherent function when the ratio of constraint to variance falls within an approximate critical windowthe paper considers whether recommendation architectures may systematically drift outside this window for certain kinds of aesthetic search. Collaborative filtering supplies high variance but limited individualized constraint. Conversational interfaces, by contrast, may enable real-time articulation of subjective preference threads, effectively increasing constraint without reducing variance. The paper does not claim that conversational systems are superior or that algorithms are obsolete. It offers a falsifiable hypothesis: that hybrid workflows-using recommendation algorithms to surface candidates and conversation to refine according to articulated criteria-may reduce search time and increase user-reported satisfaction for tasks involving niche or idiosyncratic aesthetic preferences. The framework is offered as a lens. The instrument of observation is itself part of the system under observation.

title: Automation, Learning, and Career Dynamics
affiliations: Columbia University, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, University of Texas at Austin and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Automation, Learning, and Career Dynamics
detail.abstract: We study how an automating technology affects career dynamics, human capital, and welfare in an economy where workers acquire skill through the tasks they perform. In a continuous-time general equilibrium model, learning-by-doing is determined jointly with the share of tasks automated, the frontier of tasks managers maintain, and the worker-to-manager career transition. Economies with high learning capacity admit pairs of stationary equilibria strictly ranked by the aggregate learning rate. Cheaper technology has opposite effects across the two: in the high-learning equilibrium, it raises welfare through the learning channel itself; in the low-learning equilibrium, it tips the economy into a human-capital trap. The planner's first-best combines a tax on automation profits with a subsidy on frontier-maintenance expenditures at a common rate.

title: The Cost That Changed Line Items: Complementary Inflation in the Smartphone and Mobile Data Channel
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Cost That Changed Line Items: Complementary Inflation in the Smartphone and Mobile Data Channel
detail.abstract: This paper examines, at both theoretical and descriptive levels, the claim that the hedonic quality-adjustment methodology employed in consumer price indices creates a systematic cost invisibility in certain product categories. The concept of usage complementarity is proposed and defined as the situation in which the effective utilization of a product's capability necessarily entails the consumption of another resource. The smartphone and mobile data tariff channel in Turkey is examined as a testable instance of the mechanism. Core findings are presented along three dimensions. First, the real cost per GB declined by 60-78% over the 2016-2026 period; however, according to BTK (Information Technologies and Communication Authority) data, monthly consumption per user increased approximately eightfold over the same period. Second, BTK's own quarterly reports show that owners of 4.5G-compatible devices systematically consumed more data than other users, and that this gap narrowed over time as technology diffused-a pattern consistent with capability-induced consumption growth. Third, in TÜsK's hedonic index series, the subgroup index declining by 48.29% against an actual mobile phone price increase of 2,247% between 2003 and 2022 opens to debate the scale of quality adjustment. Under the Total Real Expenditure Shift (TRES) framework, although the real cost per GB fell, the increase in consumption more than offset this decline, with total real mobile data expenditure per user rising approximately 61-92% over 2016-2026. This paper does not constitute proof; it identifies a methodology anomaly worth measuring and supports it with descriptive evidence.

title: Is Volunteering a Gateway to Increased Monetary Giving? Evidence from a Field Experiment

detail.title: Is Volunteering a Gateway to Increased Monetary Giving? Evidence from a Field Experiment

declarations.funderStatement: None

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Understanding how volunteer engagement influences subsequent charitable giving remains a central question in nonprofit management. This study employs a large-scale randomized field experiment involving over 149,000 individuals with no prior volunteering or donation to a large nonprofit organization. By comparing a group that received additional volunteer recruitment emails to a control, the research examines changes in both volunteer participation and later donation behavior. Results reveal that enhanced volunteer encouragement increases volunteer participation by 10% and subsequent donation participation by 32%, while leaving the average amount given unchanged. These findings provide robust causal evidence that volunteering elevates the likelihood of future charitable giving but does not affect per-donor giving. The study introduces an experimentally validated approach for disentangling behavioral spillovers from standard nonprofit marketing activities. Strategic implications include integrating volunteer recruitment and fundraising, highlighting optimal approaches for nonprofits to encourage both active engagement and financial support within their communities.

title:
Roles of Mass Media in Promoting Sports Betting among Nigerians:
A Study of Bet9ja & NAIRABET
affiliations: , Federal Polytechnic, Ede and Moshood Abiola Polytechnic

detail.title:
Roles of Mass Media in Promoting Sports Betting among Nigerians:
A Study of Bet9ja & NAIRABET
detail.abstract:
Mass media have become a vital tool/institution in every society of the world which cannot be ignored in the scheme of things in socio-economic and political considerations. In view of this, this paper assessed the roles played by the media in promoting sports betting among Nigerians, using two sports betting companies as examples. Using Abeokuta as study population preference, survey methodology was adopted in the data gathering with the twin use of interview guide and questionnaire as data gathering instruments. Separate interviews were conducted with media representatives of the two betting companies while 250 respondents were drawn from all areas in Abeokuta, using Stratified sampling technique combined with simple random sampling method. Results show among others that; mass media have aided the promotion of sports betting in no small measure, especially bet9ja and Nairabet, while other or say new medium of mass communication – Social media – has as well been used. The study also showed that celebrities and top-notched Nigerians were used in promoting sports betting in Nigeria. This shows that the business is not a joke or fluke. Over 88% of bettors in Abeokuta are male while about 70% are youth aged between 18-25.The study concluded that sports betting in Nigeria and mass media have enjoyed a long time companionship of mutual benefits. It was however recommended among others that other promotional strategies such as direct marketing, sponsorship, celebrity advertising, e-marketing among others will augment the continuous growth of the business in Nigeria, if well handled.

Keywords: Mass Media, Business, Economy, Sports Betting
